description: Bootstrap admin@amazai.co as a FULL-capability OWNER in the governance Directory, integrated as the platform's admin identity. Owner already holds every capability in the CAPABILITIES matrix (see directory.py), so 'full admin' == seeding an ACTIVE Owner membership for admin@amazai.co AND placing it in the owner allowlist. Two coordinated pieces: (a) a deploy-time bootstrap script (extending the scripts/provision_agents.py pattern) that writes the ACTIVE Owner MEMBER# row for the admin subject + an org.frozen-style bootstrap admin-audit row, idempotently; and (b) seeding admin@amazai.co into OWNER_SUBJECTS/OWNER_EMAILS (env-driven) so identity.assert_owner and web isOwner recognise it. CREDENTIAL CONSTRAINT (non-negotiable): do NOT write the password 'Password123!' or ANY password literal anywhere -- repo, tests, fixtures, scripts, git history. The admin's password is set at first login in Auth0 or injected out-of-band via env/secret; the user logs in as admin@amazai.co with a password they choose. Document the exact safe bootstrap procedure. The Auth0 `sub` for admin@amazai.co is not known at build time, so the identity must key on the email allowlist (OWNER_EMAILS) plus, once known, the sub -- both supported by identity.owner_emails/owner_subjects.
steps: Read scripts/provision_agents.py and scripts/deploy.sh to match the script conventions (argparse, sys.path.insert to services/, boto3 Store usage, idempotent re-run behaviour, clear refusal messages).

Create scripts/bootstrap_admin.py: a CLI that seeds admin@amazai.co as an ACTIVE Owner. It takes --email (default admin@amazai.co), an optional --subject (the Auth0 sub, when known), and --org-id (defaults to the subject or a documented single-tenant org id). It builds the row with directory.member_row(org_id, subject_or_email_placeholder, Role.OWNER, state=MemberState.ACTIVE) and writes it via Store.transact_put together with a govern.admin_audit_event(org_id, 'member.invited', actor, detail='bootstrap admin owner seeded'). It MUST be idempotent: if the MEMBER# row already exists it reports and exits 0 without a duplicate. It reads no password and writes no password. Include a module docstring documenting the safe bootstrap procedure (Auth0 sets the password at first login; OWNER_EMAILS/OWNER_SUBJECTS env gate). NOTE: because Store stamps ownerId==caller and org_id==subject today (single-tenant seam), document that in the honest-single-tenant slice the admin bootstrap seats admin@amazai.co as the Owner of its OWN org; a true cross-account admin over other owners' orgs is the deferred multi-tenant follow-up (record it in task.json deferred list, do not build it here).

Add admin@amazai.co to the documented owner allowlist wiring: extend .env.example (root) and web/.env.example with a commented example line showing OWNER_EMAILS=admin@amazai.co (and OWNER_SUBJECTS=<auth0-sub-once-known>) and VITE_OWNER_EMAIL=admin@amazai.co, with a comment that these are set at deploy time, never a password. Do NOT invent a new env var name -- reuse the existing OWNER_SUBJECTS/OWNER_EMAILS/VITE_OWNER_SUB/VITE_OWNER_EMAIL that identity.owner_subjects/owner_emails and auth0.isOwner already read.

Document the full bootstrap procedure in docs/ (a new docs/ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP.md or a section appended to CLOUDSHELL.md / README.md admin section -- pick the one most consistent with existing docs): create the admin@amazai.co user in Auth0 (password set there by the human at first login, never in the repo), set OWNER_EMAILS=admin@amazai.co (+ OWNER_SUBJECTS once the sub is known) and VITE_OWNER_EMAIL for the console build, then run scripts/bootstrap_admin.py to seat the ACTIVE Owner row. Explicitly state that no password is stored anywhere and that the user logs in with the password they set in Auth0.

Add tests/test_bootstrap_admin.py (moto-backed, using the `table`/`store` fixtures): assert the script's seeding function (factor the row-building into an importable function, e.g. bootstrap_admin.seed_owner(store, org_id, subject) returning the rows) writes an ACTIVE Owner MEMBER# row whose Membership resolves via directory.membership_of to Role.OWNER + MemberState.ACTIVE; assert directory.can(that_membership, cap) is True for EVERY Capability in directory.CAPABILITIES (proving 'full admin'); assert re-running is idempotent (no duplicate / no crash); assert an admin-audit row was written. Include a test that greps the produced rows and asserts NO field contains a password-like literal (belt-and-braces on the credential constraint).

Add a repo-wide guard test (or extend an existing meta test) asserting the string 'Password123!' does not appear anywhere under services/, scripts/, tests/, web/src/, docs/ -- so the constraint is enforced by the suite, not just by review. Implement it by walking the tree and reading files (skip binary/node_modules/.venv/dist), asserting the literal is absent.
Run the full suite and the three build checks; confirm green (only the 3 pre-existing failures).
acceptance_criteria: scripts/bootstrap_admin.py exists, is idempotent, seeds an ACTIVE Owner MEMBER# row + an admin-audit row for admin@amazai.co, and reads/writes NO password.
A test proves the seeded membership holds every capability in directory.CAPABILITIES (full admin) and that re-running does not duplicate.
A suite-level guard test proves the literal 'Password123!' appears nowhere in the tracked source tree.
.env.example / web/.env.example document OWNER_EMAILS/OWNER_SUBJECTS/VITE_OWNER_EMAIL for admin@amazai.co with no password.
A docs page documents the exact safe bootstrap procedure (Auth0-set password, env allowlist, run the script).
`.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` green apart from the 3 pre-existing failures; infra synth and web build pass.
verification: grep -rn 'Password123' services scripts tests web/src docs  (must return nothing)
cd infra && npx cdk synth > /dev/null  (exit 0); cd web && npm run build && test -f dist/index.html
findings: Committed as 21cbcf8 (source-only; no __pycache__/*.pyc in the commit). Delivered scripts/bootstrap_admin.py with an importable seed_owner(store, org_id, subject) that writes the ACTIVE Owner MEMBER# row + a govern.admin_audit_event('member.invited', detail='bootstrap admin owner seeded') atomically via store.transact_put, idempotent (returns [] and writes nothing if the row exists). CREDENTIAL CONSTRAINT honored: no password literal anywhere. NOTE on the guard test: Python constant-folds adjacent string-literal concatenation, so the assembled forbidden string leaked into the .pyc and `grep -rn Password123 tests` matched the bytecode cache; fixed by building it with ''.join([...]) of char fragments (not constant-folded), so neither source nor .pyc contains the literal. Env wiring reused existing names OWNER_EMAILS/OWNER_SUBJECTS (root .env.example, read by identity.assert_owner from Lambda env) and VITE_OWNER_EMAIL (web/.env.example, read by auth0.isOwner) - no new var invented. Docs: new docs/ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP.md. Verification: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest` = 1226 passed / 3 failed (the 3 pre-existing tests/test_gaps_api.py failures only; +8 new tests over the 1218 baseline). `grep -rn Password123 services scripts tests web/src docs` returns nothing (exit 1). `cd infra && npx cdk synth` exit 0. `cd web && npm run build` exit 0, dist/index.html present, `grep -c demoApi dist/assets/*.js` == 0. Multi-tenant cross-account admin over other owners' orgs was NOT built (single-tenant seam: bootstrap seats admin@amazai.co as Owner of its own org); documented as the deferred follow-up in docs/ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP.md.
